title: My comeback has a purpose
author: Matthew Ehsan
paragraphs: I started my athletic journey on a basketball court. Then I fell in love with powerlifting, where steady work became measurable progress and eventually helped me break multiple records at McKinney High School. After two years of building my strength, my parents agreed to let me play football. I joined the varsity team, played several positions, and eventually became one of its captains. I loved the responsibility of showing up for my teammates and being part of something bigger than myself.

Injuries changed the direction of that journey. A shoulder injury required surgery, and a severe injury to my little finger brought me into the care of multiple orthopedic specialists, including my cousin, Dr. Sam Ehsan, an orthopedic and hand surgeon. I began to understand how much an injury can take from an athlete beyond physical performance. Confidence, independence, identity, and the feeling of belonging to a team can all be affected. Those experiences gave injury prevention and rehabilitation a meaning that no scoreboard could teach me.

Today, I am studying kinesiology at Texas Tech University with the goal of attending medical school and becoming a physician in sports medicine or physical medicine and rehabilitation, also known as PM&R. I want to understand the biomechanics of movement, the physiology of training, and the science of tissue healing. Just as importantly, I want to learn how to listen to an injured athlete, recognize the emotional weight of recovery, and help build a safe, individualized path forward. My experiences have given me motivation. Education, research literacy, clinical training, and service must turn that motivation into the knowledge and judgment a physician needs.

With support from my father, Alex Ehsan, MD, PhD, Sam Ehsan, MD, in orthopedics and hand surgery, and Pasha Ehsan, MD, in physical medicine and rehabilitation, I am building this student athlete education initiative. Our purpose is to make evidence-based information about injury prevention, recovery, and athlete wellbeing easier to understand. As a student, my role is to learn, organize resources, and connect athletes with reliable education while medical guidance remains with qualified professionals.

To the athlete who is hurting, I want you to know that your value has never depended on your last lift, your place on the depth chart, or how quickly you return to play. You deserve time to heal, people who listen, and a future that remains full of possibility. My comeback is taking a new direction. I want to carry what sports gave me into medicine and use what injury taught me to help other athletes protect the futures they are working so hard to build.
editorial_note: First-person narrative prepared from the family account supplied by Alex Ehsan. No specific shoulder procedure, record totals, completed research, clinical experience or recovery outcome added.
